## Added

- `model`: a storey that drew nothing now says so. A sheet whose fills the
  rules cannot read still yields a storey — the levels are parameters, the
  slab falls back to the outline of whatever was found — and until now that
  came back looking like a reconstruction: a floor of 0.4 m² with no rooms and
  no walls, a roof outline of 0.2 m². Such a storey is carried as it came and
  marked `empty` (`model.floors[].empty`, and in the report's `floors[]`), with
  a `warnings` entry naming the page and what the sheet gave; a roof outline
  under 2 m² is marked the same way. Nothing is dropped and no geometry
  changes: a caller that draws a building now knows which storeys are not one.
  Across the corpus this marks the only storey of dossiers 3 and 12, both
  storeys of 14, one of the four in 11 — with its 0.19 m² roof outline, and
  dossier 3's 0.58 m² one — and one storey each in 5, 9 and 13; the reference
  dossier and the sketch set are untouched. A storey that is small but not
  hollow is not marked: the rule asks only what the sheet drew, so dossier 11's
  three 7 m² floors, which do draw rooms, stand as they are.
